rejected.title: Managing water sustainably
card: Managing water sustainably means using water so there is enough for people and nature now and in the future. Every home, school and community can help.
Collecting
A rainwater tank collects rain from a roof. The water can be used on gardens or to flush toilets, so less tap water is needed.
Reducing
Fixing leaks, taking shorter showers and planting water-wise gardens all cut the amount of water used. Water-wise gardens use plants that need little water.
Reusing
Grey water is used water from showers, baths, basins and washing machines. It can be reused on lawns and flower beds instead of going straight down the drain.
rejected.remember: Save water by collecting it, using less of it and reusing it.

a.q: A school wants to use less tap water on its garden beds. Which action does this best?
opts: Connect a rainwater tank to the garden taps
Water the beds each day in the same way
Plant more lawn that needs regular watering
Wash the school's paths with a hose each week
a.why: A tank collects rain, so the garden needs less tap water. The other options keep using tap water or use even more of it.
a.clue: Which choice collects water that would otherwise run away?

b.q: Priya's family in Tamworth reuses water from their washing machine on their flower beds. What is this water called, and why does it help?
opts: Grey water, because it is reused instead of wasted
Grey water, because it is collected from the roof
Rainwater, because it is reused instead of wasted
Rainwater, because it is collected from the roof
b.why: Water from a washing machine is grey water, and reusing it means less tap water is needed. The tempting pair with the roof gets the term right but the reason wrong: rain from a roof is rainwater, not grey water.
b.clue: Think about where the water first came from: a roof or a washing machine?

problems.detail: The scenario shows untreated washing-machine water put on a vegetable patch as good practice. NSW Health greywater guidance advises against using untreated greywater on vegetables eaten raw, such as leafy greens and root crops, so this could teach an unsafe habit. A flower bed or lawn would be a safer setting.
